title: SAST Triage Verdict
description: Layer-2 structured output schema. The triage LLM MUST return one object per Layer-1 finding. Enforced via function-calling / JSON mode so the model retries on mismatch.

id.description: Finding id carried over from Layer 1 (e.g. F032).

verdict.description: Is the flagged code genuinely a vulnerability? TRUE_POSITIVE = real vulnerable pattern; FALSE_POSITIVE = rule error / effectively mitigated / not applicable; NEEDS_REVIEW = context-dependent, requires human or dynamic confirmation.

exploitability.description: Realistic exploitability given sanitizers, guards, and preconditions actually present in the code.

reachable.description: Is the sink reachable from an external entry point (mounted route / handler)? 'false' for training snippets, dead code, or non-runtime files.

priority.description: Derived triage priority. P1 = reachable TP, HIGH exploit. P2 = reachable TP, MED. P3 = LOW/among mitigated or unreachable TP, or NEEDS_REVIEW with impact. P4 = FP or informational hardening.

category.description: Normalized weakness class, e.g. sql-injection, path-traversal, code-injection, hardcoded-secret, open-redirect, info-disclosure, iac-misconfig, ci-hardening, supply-chain.

rationale.description: One-to-three sentence reasoning for the verdict. Must reference the concrete code, not restate the rule.

evidence.description: The specific code fact that supports the verdict (the exact source, sink, sanitizer, or guard). A verdict without evidence is invalid.

suggested_fix.description: Concrete remediation, ideally the parameterized / validated form.

triage_note.description: Nuance a rule engine cannot see: mitigations present, training-snippet vs live route, duplicate-of, by-design, etc.
